title: theoryforge theory object
description: Language-agnostic source of truth for a theory as a versioned, machine-checkable object. Authored as YAML, validated against this JSON Schema, read/written identically by the R and Python packages.
$comment: Closed at the top level: a misspelt collection key (predicitions) would otherwise be accepted while silently dropping the collection and changing every downstream verdict. Item objects stay open so individual entries can carry extra metadata.

schema_version.description: major.minor version of the theory schema. validate() requires it and validate(full) checks its pattern, but neither package gates loading on the version.

maturity.description: At draft maturity the gate is advisory: failed blocker items are still reported as fail and still count in the aggregate score, but the gate never reads blocked.

theory_form.description: Declared form of the theory, validated against the enum. No score depends on it: the checklist applies the same twelve items to every form.

type.description: What the prediction asserts. existence: that an effect or relation exists, without a direction. directional: a sign or an order, including comparisons, interactions, the invariance of a direction across groups and claims that an effect occurs only when a condition holds. interval: that a quantity lies in a stated range, the range the theory permits. point: one value, with the tolerance that measurement requires (the width is measurement tolerance, not latitude the theory allows). Riskiness ordering: existence < directional < interval < point. The label is self-declared, and no function checks it against the statement.

risk_score.description: Informational, read by no function. The risk_score that severity() reports is derived from the type.

severity.description: A declared pre-data severity of the claim, from 0 to 1. The checklist's risk_severity item reads it, and uses the claim-form rubric of severity() for a prediction that declares none.

bounds.description: The region of the quantity the claim allows. A null or infinite bound is open, so a one-sided claim leaves one side null. post_data_severity() reads it with each test outcome's estimate and se. Full validation also requires at least one finite bound and lower not above upper.

unit.description: What n_planned counts, such as participants or items.

sesoi.description: The smallest effect of interest. Full validation also requires a finite value.

sesoi_scale.description: The scale of sesoi, such as ms or Cohen's d.

decision_probability.description: The planned probability of a decision other than power, such as that of an interval estimate falling outside a region of practical equivalence.

power_lo.description: The lower end of an interval around the stated power or decision probability, such as the Wilson interval of a simulated power. Full validation also requires power_lo not above power_hi.

power_hi.description: The upper end of that interval.

method.description: How the power or decision probability was obtained, such as simulation or an analytic formula.

design_ref.description: A file, DOI or URL of the design analysis, such as a pilotr specification or power report.

test.description: The sampling plan for testing the prediction, which a Stage 1 Registered Report states for each hypothesis. It is recorded, not scored: power does not raise the severity of a claim (Meehl, 1967), though it decides how informative a failed test is (Lakens, 2022). preregister() lists it after the hypotheses, and no other function reads it. The interval a claim allows belongs in bounds.

auxiliary_assumptions.description: The Lakatosian protective belt, represented as first-class versioned entities.

added_for.description: A null value marks a core assumption. Otherwise, it is the id of the prediction whose anomaly the assumption was added to answer. The amendment appraisal counts such an assumption as ad hoc unless one of the predictions it protects is new in the amended version, differs from this one and is corroborated.

protects.description: The ids of the predictions the assumption shields from refutation. Only a prediction new in an amended version, other than added_for, can clear an assumption added for an anomaly.

test_outcomes.description: Links a registered prediction to its realized result.

registered.description: Where the test was preregistered, such as an OSF registration. The amendment appraisal reads it only to report which corroborations were preregistered, and no verdict depends on it.

estimate.description: The estimate the test observed, on the scale of its prediction's bounds. Full validation also requires a finite value.

se.description: The standard error of the estimate. Full validation also requires a finite value.
